lede: Detroit had last change, so Todd McLellan picked most of these matchups. Detroit played without Sheldon Dries and Carter Mazur. Vancouver played without Brendan Gallagher and Elias Pettersson.

notes.head: The third line drew Rossi’s line
notes.text: Todd McLellan sent Kasper, Finnie and Arvidsson out for 8:19 of their 10:51 at 5-on-5 against Öhgren, Rossi and Lekkerimäki (77%, about 21% with no line matching), and they had the better of the chances, 0.79 to 0.61 expected goals. Detroit scored two of its five goals then.

notes.head: The fourth line drew Cotter’s line
notes.text: Appleton, Rasmussen and Kolesar spent 9:23 of their 12:36 at 5-on-5 against Reinhardt, Quillan and Cotter (74%, about 26% with no line matching), and they had the better of the chances, 0.48 to 0.15 expected goals. The only Vancouver goal came then.

notes.head: DeBrincat’s line drew Boeser’s line
notes.text: DeBrincat, Copp and Raymond spent 11:20 of their 15:33 at 5-on-5 against DeBrusk, Chytil and Boeser (73%, about 27% with no line matching), and they had the better of the chances, 0.68 to 0.45 expected goals.

notes.head: One matchup went wrong
notes.text: Brandsegg-Nygård, Dach and Compher kept drawing Vancouver’s third line, O'Connor, Mueller and Karlsson. In those 9:00 Vancouver had 0.74 expected goals to Detroit’s 0.32.

foot: Todd McLellan matched harder than in his other home games: each line spent 72% of its time against one opposing line, against 33% to 56% in his last ten.
